page.layout: One printed page (left of the scan), one column of running text, German glosses in black letter. Page number and running head at the top. The right edge of the printed page is cut off by the scan edge. A catchword stands at the lower right.

main_text.l: paralysis, die Zucht[?] / modestia, die Flucht / fuga, die
Wasserfucht / hydrops, die Forcht / timor, die Last / o-
nus, die Lust / astutia, die Kunst / ars, die Frist / tempus,
die Lust / delectatio, die Brust / pectus, die Schwulst / tu-
mor, die Wurst / farcime, die Gestalt / species, die Welt /
mundus, die Geduld / patientia, die Art / natura, die Fart /
expeditio, die Geburt / nativitas, die Angst / angustia,
die Vernunft / ratio, die Zunft / tribus, die Zukunft /
adventus, die Axt / securis,
die Donaw / Danubius. Et
alia quaedam.
Cujus nota est articulus das: ut, das Testament.
Primo, Nomina oppidorum, pagorum, literarum
& syllabarum: ut, das Leipzig / Lipsia, das Basel /
Basilea, das Ulm / das Ja / das Nein. Excipitur
die Lippe / urbs Lippia, & alia quaedam. Deinde desi-
nentia in ment, nis, len vel lin, & alia nonnulla: ut
das Sacrament / Sacramentum, das Gezeugnis / te-
stimonium, das Gefängnis / carcer, das Männlein /
masculus, das Fräulein / mulierecula, das Grab /
sepulchrum, das Weib / mulier, das Kalb / vitulus, das
Lamb / agnus, das Bad / balneum, das Rad / rota, das
Augenglied / gena, das Glied / membrum, das Lied /
canticum, das Leid / luctus, das Wild / fera, das Bild /
imago, das Gold / aurum, das Band / vinculum, das Land /
regio, das Pfand / pignus, das Kind / infans, das Rind /
bos, das End / finis, das Elend / miseria, das Pfund /
libra, das Pferd / equus, das Felsen[?] / rus, das Schaf / ovis,
das Schaff / vas, das Schiff / navis, das Dorff / pagus,
das Ding / res, das Bedüng / conditio, das Dach / tectum,
das Fach / interstitium, das Gemach / conclave, das Gelach
/ symposium, das Pech / pix, das Blech / lamina, das Loch
/ foramen, das Block / truncus, das Joch / jugum, das Fleisch

page.notes: The right-hand part of the printed page is cut off by the edge of the scan, so the ends of lines from about "Basilea" onward, and the words after "Lipsia", are incomplete or missing. Words broken off at the scan edge are given only as far as they are visible; nothing has been added. Several German glosses in black letter are doubtful (marked [?]), notably "Zucht", "Felsen" and "Bedüng". The bottom catchword is only partly visible at the edge. A large part of the right-hand text continues beyond the scan, so the transcription of this page is incomplete on the right. The left margin is clean and has no marginal notes.
